title: Forensic Escalation and Capacity Hedging Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines a combined forensic-escalation and capacity-hedging procedure for production incidents that threaten SLOs for inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments). It codifies: escalation responsibilities, evidence collection standards for post-incident review, automated and manual capacity hedging actions, and an error-budget-aware decision matrix for graceful degradation. This doc is intended for SREs on-call, on-call leads, runtime engineers, and incident commanders.

Scope and applicability:

- Services in scope: inference-router, batch-scheduler, kv-cache-service, model-runtime-pool, burst-absorber, traffic-router.
- Environments: prod (all regions), pre-prod only when configured with production traffic mirroring.
- This playbook applies when any of the following SLOs are at risk: 99th-percentile latency, p95 latency > SLO, availability (5xx rate), or sustained error-budget burn.

Quick reference (TL;DR):

1) If an alert indicates SLO degradation and burn rate > 3x sustained for 10m, declare a Sev-2 and execute hedging steps A–C.
2) If burn rate > 5x in a 30m window or p99 latency > 3x SLO, declare Sev-1 and escalate to oncall lead + infra lead; begin emergency capacity hedging and traffic reroute.
3) Collect forensic evidence in parallel (traces, key metrics, GPU utilization, server-side logs, KV hit-rate snapshots).

Escalation matrix and ownership:

- First responder (on-call SRE): initial triage, apply pre-authorized hedging actions, collect evidence.
- On-call lead: decision to elevate to Sev-1, coordinate cross-team owners, approve cost-impacting hedges.
- Runtime infra owner: responsible for executing pool scale-ups, patch rollbacks, and kernel toggles.
- Product impact lead: assesses functional degradation risk and communicates to customer-success as needed.

Decision triggers (mapping of SLO telemetry to actions):

- Trigger A (Early warning): p95 latency > 0.8 * SLO for 15m OR error_budget_burn_rate >= 2x for 30m. Action: enable additional batching (soft), increase batch-scheduler backlog limit +10%, refresh KV cache nodes. Owner: on-call SRE. Cooldown: 10m. Estimated cost impact: low.

- Trigger B (Hedging): p95 latency > SLO OR error_budget_burn_rate >= 3x sustained for 10m. Action: scale model-runtime-pool by +1-2 nodes (hot spare), divert 10% traffic to fallback-quantized model variant, temporarily enable degraded features (noncritical append-only logging disabled). Owner: runtime infra. Cooldown: 30m. Estimated cost impact: medium.

- Trigger C (Emergency): p99 latency > 3x SLO OR error_budget_burn_rate >= 5x in 30m OR 10% of hosts return 5xx. Action: immediate cross-region reroute to standby region, provision burst-absorber instances, engage sales/customer-success for affected tenants. Owner: on-call lead + infra. Cooldown: 60m. Estimated cost impact: high.

Forensic evidence collection checklist (must run in parallel with hedging):

1) Snap telemetry window: persist time-series from -30m to +30m for: p50/p95/p99 latency, req/sec, dropped-requests/sec, 5xx-rate, request queue length, GPU util per-device, KV hit rate.
2) Trace capture: increase sampled trace capture to 100% for affected request IDs for 15 minutes.
3) Kernel and runtime logs: collect last 200 lines of worker logs, scheduler logs, and docker/runtime stderr.
4) Memory/GPU dumps: if OOM suspected, capture nvprof or equivalent stack traces (rotate to S3 with path: s3://forensic-dumps/{incident-id}/).
5) Config snapshot: save routing policies, autoscale config, and kernel flags to git tag incident-{id}-config.

Standardized evidence manifest (example – save as incident-{id}-manifest.json):

{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-1234",
  "start_ts": "2026-01-19T13:42:00Z",
  "services": ["inference-router", "model-runtime-pool"],
  "artifacts": ["/s3/forensic-dumps/INC-2026-1234/traces.zip", "/s3/forensic-dumps/INC-2026-1234/gpu-profiles.tar.gz"]
}

(Keep incident manifests as immutable artifacts for retro.)

Runbook: head-to-toe operational steps (numbered):

1) Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty within 2 minutes.
2) Collect the forensic evidence per checklist.
3) Read the incident dashboard and validate SLOs at risk. Use the following commands to get immediate state:
   - rdc metrics query --service inference-router --window 30m --agg p95,p99
   - rictl pool list --name model-runtime-pool --region us-west-2
   - redwood-trace export --filter "http.status_code >= 500" --since 15m --out /tmp/trace-500.json
4) Apply Trigger A actions if applicable. Monitor 5m for improvements.
5) If no improvement and Trigger B conditions met, apply hedging: run rictl scale-pool --pool model-runtime-pool --delta +2 --reason "INC-{id} hedging" and redwood-router reroute --policy fallback-quantized --percent 10. Notify runtime infra.
6) For Trigger C, escalate to oncall lead and run: rictl provision burst-absorber --region us-west-2 --count 4 && traffic-router shift --to-region us-east-1 --percent 50. Inform postmortem leads and customer-success.
7) Once stabilized, start gradual rollback: decrease hedges in reverse order with cooldown checks (p95 < 0.9*SLO for 20m).

Rollback and canary guidance:

- All hedging actions must have a rollback plan documented before change.
- Rollback cadence: stepwise with 15–30m observation windows. Do not remove region-level hedges until p99 < 1.2*SLO for 1h.

Template: hedging action record (create at start of hedging):

- incident_id: INC-YYYY-NNNN
- action: scale-pool / reroute / degrade-feature
- owner: team name
- expected-metrics: p95 drop to < target
- rollback-criteria: p95 < 0.9*SLO for 20m
- cost-estimate: low/medium/high

Operational tooling and automation primitives:

- rictl (runtime infra CLI): scale-pool, provision, drain-host, disable-kernel-flag. Example: rictl scale-pool --pool model-runtime-pool --delta +2 --origin incident-INC-2026-1234.
- redwood-router: reroute, degrade-feature, set-traffic-split. Example: redwood-router reroute --policy degrade-noncritical --percent 20.
- telemetry snapshot: rdc snapshot --services inference-router,model-runtime-pool --out s3://forensic-dumps/INC-2026-1234/metrics.json
- playbook orchestration: incident-bot add-note "hedge applied: +2 model-runtime" and incident-bot run checklist forensic-collect.

Table: Hedging actions matrix (text table)

| Trigger | Primary action | Owner | Cooldown | Cost impact | Rollback signal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A (early) | Increase batch backlog +10%, refresh KV nodes | on-call SRE | 10m | Low | p95 < 0.9*SLO / 15m |
| B (hedge) | Scale runtime +1-2, 10% fallback model | runtime infra | 30m | Medium | p95 < 0.9*SLO / 30m |
| C (emergency) | Cross-region reroute, burst-absorber | on-call lead | 60m | High | p99 < 1.5*SLO / 60m |

Incident review standards (for postmortem):

- Evidence completeness: incident manifest, telemetry windows, trace sets, config snapshot, and action log. Missing artifacts reduce severity for follow-up items.
- Timeline fidelity: all state changes must be committed to the incident timeline with timestamps and actor. Use the standard template: detection -> triage -> actions -> stabilization -> rollback -> retro start.
- Forensic rubric for root cause categories: 1) Code/regression (deploy-induced), 2) Capacity-constraint (queueing/backpressure), 3) Data/traffic-change (input distribution), 4) External dependency failure. Each postmortem must classify primary and contributing causes.

Reliability initiatives and follow-up (post-incident):

- If incident consumed > 50% of monthly error budget or required emergency actions, initiate a Reliability Initiative (RI) with: hypothesis, measurable goals (SLO improvement), M&E plan, and owner. Example RI: "KV caching strategy for tail latency" with goal p99 reduce 40% in 3 months.
- Cost-accounting: log actual hedging cost and reconcile to finance tagging.
- Automate: if a hedging action resolved problem two times in 90 days, schedule an automation project to make the hedge safe and reversible by a single CLI command with pre-approved budget limits.

Playbook examples and sample incident narrative (abridged):

- Incident: sudden p95 spike in inference-router on 2026-01-15 04:40 UTC.
- On-call executed Trigger A (batch backlog increase), no improvement. Trigger B executed: +2 runtime nodes and 15% traffic reroute to fallback-quantized. Forensic captures showed a KV eviction storm; postmortem triggered RI to refactor cache shard placement.

Appendix: useful commands and dashboards

- Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/slo/inference-overview, https://dashboards.redwood.internal/forensics/INC-{id}
- Commands: rictl scale-pool --pool model-runtime-pool --delta +2
           redwood-router reroute --policy fallback-quantized --percent 10
           rdc snapshot --services inference-router --window 60m --out /s3/forensic-dumps/INC-{id}/metrics.json

Checklist to close the incident (must be completed before postmortem):

- [ ] Incident timeline recorded and verified by oncall lead.
- [ ] Evidence manifest uploaded to S3.
- [ ] All hedges returned to normal or documented as permanent mitigations.
- [ ] Postmortem created and assigned within 72 hours.
- [ ] Reliability Initiative created if threshold exceeded.

- 2025-12-08: Added evidence manifest schema and automation primitives (reviewers: Marcus Nguyen, Leah Gomez).
